keyTakeaways: A theatre can make mobile surtitles repeatable by keeping a small pool of managed loan phones.
Front-of-house staff can hand over a ready Viewer page and give simple language instructions.
Charging, network access, brightness, privacy, spares and an auditorium test matter as much as the software.
SurtitleLive connects prepared subtitle material to a browser; it does not provide phones, networks, translators or compliance certification.

faq.question: Can a theatre provide phones for audience surtitles?
faq.answer: Yes. A venue can keep a small pool of charged, numbered loan phones, open the correct Viewer page before doors open and hand them out through its audience-service team. It can also offer a QR code or short link for people who prefer to use their own phone.

faq.question: Do audience members need to install an app?
faq.answer: No. SurtitleLive Viewer works in a browser. An audience member can open a link or scan a QR code, choose an available language and read the prepared surtitles without installing a dedicated audience app.

faq.question: What should a theatre prepare before offering loan phones?
faq.answer: Charge and number the phones, test the network and the correct show page, confirm the available languages, prepare a few spares, and test brightness, reflections and reading angles in the auditorium. Staff should also rehearse a short handover explanation.

faq.question: Are mobile surtitles a complete accessibility service?
faq.answer: No. They are one delivery option. A theatre may also need projected surtitles, professional captioning, sign-language interpretation, hearing-assistance systems or other services. SurtitleLive does not certify that a particular arrangement meets every accessibility or legal requirement.

glossary.definition: A venue-owned phone that is charged, configured, checked and issued to an audience member for a performance.
The audience-facing theatre team that prepares, hands over and collects devices and explains the service.
The browser-based audience view where prepared subtitle material can be read on a phone.
Prepared theatre surtitles delivered to a spectator's own phone or to a phone supplied by the venue.
An arrangement in which spectators use their own phones through a QR code or short link instead of a loan device.
